title: MapLibre GL JS vs Mapbox GL JS
deck: The fork measured against the code it forked from. mapbox-gl 1.13.3, the last BSD-licensed Mapbox release, beside maplibre-gl 5.24.0 and 6.7.0, all three fed the same self-hosted Berlin tiles, style, sprites and glyphs in one pinned Chromium on one GPU: startup timeline, frame time cold and warm, memory.
trademarks: Mapbox and Mapbox GL JS are trademarks of Mapbox, Inc. mapbox-gl 1.13.3 is used under its BSD-3-Clause license.
MapLibre is a project of the MapLibre organization; maplibre-gl is BSD-3-Clause.

Map data: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL, via the Geofabrik Berlin extract of 2026-01-01, cut with planetiler. Style: OSM Bright by OpenMapTiles, BSD-3-Clause. Glyphs: Noto Sans, SIL Open Font License.
limitations: One GPU, one operating system, one browser build: an integrated AMD Radeon on Windows 11 in Playwright's Chromium headless shell. Ratios on Apple silicon, on a discrete NVIDIA card, or in Firefox will differ.

Renderer only. Mapbox's hosted data, the Standard style, its CDN and its current SDK are not measured, because Mapbox's Product Terms forbid using current Mapbox GL JS in a comparison with a substitute; the Mapbox candidate is the last BSD-licensed release, which is also the code MapLibre forked.
One style, OSM Bright, with no globe, terrain, hillshade or 3D buildings, so features one build has and another lacks are not exercised.

MapLibre GL JS 6 changed the default of zoomLevelsToOverscale to 4, so past the source's maxzoom of 14 it fetches and parses each parent tile once per child position (four requests per parent at z16) to place labels differently. That is the shipped default and is measured as such; the tile request counts per pass are in the run file, and the parity gate counts distinct features on screen so this tiling choice does not fail it.
Frame time is unthrottled and headless: relative renderer cost per frame with the camera moving every frame, not what a 60 Hz screen shows a user.
Memory is renderer plus GPU process private bytes over a blank page; GPU-dedicated memory is not separately measured, and the JS heap figure includes workers only where the browser reports it.
mapbox-gl 1.13.3 renders through WebGL 1 and the MapLibre builds through WebGL 2, because that is what each artifact does; nothing was patched to equalize it.
Fifteen passes on one machine on one day; every sample is in the run file.
